content.comment_body: Hello, I'm currently running 5 [product_name] controllers ([article_no]) with each a [product_name] DM16 and DM8 expansion module in my home setup. This provides 20 digital inputs and 16 digital outputs per controller, across 5 units. I read about the new [product_name] ([article_no]), which reportedly supports communication with up to 8 other controllers. I thought this could allow a single master program to control all units, with the others acting as slaves, and potentially expand my home automation further. Can each of the (up to 8) [product_name] controllers in a master-slave configuration have DM16 and DM8 expansion modules? The product brochure mentions: "The theoretical degree of expansion of a [product_name] configuration is thus 88 digital inputs, 80 digital outputs, 64 analog inputs, and 18 analog outputs." It also states that slave devices can be equipped with proven expansion modules, up to the max process image. So, my main question is: can I run five (or even eight) [product_name] ([article_no]) units, each with DM16 and DM8 expansions, in a master-slave configuration?

You can use four [product_name] ([article_no]) controllers with DM16 and DM8 expansions. That’s because one [product_name] controller with DM16 and DM8 modules has 20 digital inputs. 4 controllers x 20 digital inputs = 80 digital inputs, and the maximum allowed is 88.

Feedback indicates there are limits on digital inputs but doesn't fully clarify whether their ideal expanded configuration is practical, leaving some questions about the total expansion possible.
